_comment: Recorded by scripts/bench.py --save. `make bench` compares against this and fails on a regression worse than 10% (AGENTS.md §8). Commit a regenerated file with the change that caused it.
_residency: Checked with scripts/bench.py --residency on 2026-10-10, 12 open/highlight/close cycles per size. The residue after close is NOT a per-line leak: at 8 MiB the heap is flat at 174.1 KiB across all 11 post-warmup cycles (0.0 KiB variation). At 4 MiB it oscillates between 174.1 and 142.1 KiB forever -- a collect-when-over-a-threshold allocator, not accumulation -- so per-cycle deltas alternate sign and are not a trend. This supersedes the earlier '~0.2 bytes per highlighted line' characterisation, which came from reading one close of one file and could not distinguish a leak from a floor.
_lua_base: lua_base rose from 92.1 KiB to ~122.7 KiB when data/core/memory.lua (the core:memory report) was added and became reachable through require. It is Lua source now resident, paid once at startup, and is why 'lua after close' reads +2.7% rather than 0.0%. It is not growth per file and does not scale with document size -- compare lua_close across sizes, not the residue.
_timings: The load/highlight seconds in this file were recorded on an otherwise idle machine. A ~25% regression reported against them on a busy machine (Chrome resident) reproduced across best-of-5 but is machine load, not code: the measurement runs the pure-Lua data layer under `lua`, which links none of the C that changed. Re-record with --save on a quiet machine before treating a timing regression as real.
